title: Making a plan you can carry out

D0.outcome: Explains a plan as a direction supported by a feature of the position that the available pieces can carry out, revised when the opponent changes the position.

D1.outcome: For each side in a quiet position, names one plan that follows from a feature of the position (weak pawn, open file, space).

D2.outcome: In unlabeled positions, picks a move that belongs to a feasible plan and rejects a plan the available pieces cannot carry out.

D3.outcome: Explains why a plan fails when its feasibility condition breaks, and does not change plans without a reason.

misconceptions: Having a plan means pushing a pawn.
An unsound plan is better than none (not adopted).
sources: sources/sheets/edlasker_chess-strategy.md §4 K33; §7 row 'Plan vs none' (not adopted)
conditions: A plan is large-scale, promises success, is feasible with the means at hand, and advances only when concerted piece action can follow.
A plan is a general direction plus a guess at the opponent's main counter-moves, revised from time to time.
contrasts: 'an unsound plan carried through is better than no plan' (dated coaching advice).
A forced tactical position where no plan is needed.

soft_prereq_notes.OPN.SETUP.D1: an opening setup is a first plan
